data.source_title: Observed rates of surgical instrument errors point to visualization tasks as being a critically vulnerable point in sterile processing and a significant cause of lost chargeable OR minutes
data.locator: Methods and Results; directly observed surgical instrument errors, case delays and delay duration
data.source_setting: Seven pediatric operating rooms at a two-hospital academic healthcare campus; elective OR days
data.source_period: Summer 2021; observation shifts during elective surgery days
data.source_n: 24 trained student observers; 236 errors in 147 cases; delay status documented for 103 of 147 error cases
data.quantity: Cases affected by delays and average delay time among cases with delay documentation
data.source_evidence_basis: Direct observers recorded 236 instrument errors across 147 cases. For the 103 cases with delay status documented, over half of inpatient and outpatient cases had delays; average time lost per case was 10.16 minutes.
data.limitations: Delay status was missing for 44/147 cases with errors; sampling occurred in pediatric ORs and may not represent adult or RWJ operations. The study estimates delays, not stockout probability or sterile-processing turnaround time.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Use as an external illustration that missing/broken/contaminated instruments can pause setup or operative progress. Do not apply its delay mean to RWJ or interpret it as instrument processing time.
